summary.headline: Concord Biotech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR257 crores, with EBITDA margin at 32% and PAT at INR58 crores.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached INR257 crores (+26% YoY), led by API at INR219 crores (+42%) while formulations fell 23% to INR39 crores, which management attributed to lost Middle East supplies. Exports grew 46% and domestic grew 12%. EBITDA rose 34% to INR82 crores (32% margin, +190 bps), and gross margin was 78.9%. Management said part of the growth was spillover from Q4 FY26 procurement delays, and that the injectable facility and Stellon Biotech are still at a nascent stage.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR219 crores, up 42% YoY. Growth reported across immunosuppressants, anti-infectives, oncology and antifungals; anti-infectives and oncology grew faster than immunosuppressants.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR39 crores, down 23% YoY. Management attributed the decline to Middle East customers buying API instead of formulation in Q1; ex-Middle East, domestic double-digit growth in both Intra (nephrology) and INCA (critical care) divisions.

segments.name: CDMO (fermentation)
segments.commentary: Currently about 1-2% of revenue. One product commercialised in animal health (US, ANDA), currently a couple of million dollars in sales; management aims for double-digit share over time.

segments.name: Injectables
segments.commentary: Facility commercialised; utilisation about 5% in the quarter. Own branded generics supplied in-house; contract manufacturing discussions advanced, with some commercial onboarding expected in 2H FY27. Emerging-market sales expected from next year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects growth in FY27 to exceed the company's historical growth rates, citing visibility for coming quarters.
Spillover from Q4 FY26 procurement delays expected to continue into subsequent quarters; not quantified.
Long-term view: INR3,000 crores revenue from existing infrastructure in about 5-6 years, split roughly INR600-700 crores formulations and INR2,200 crores API.
EBITDA margin expected to exceed sales growth in FY27; 40% margin target expected to be reached partly in FY27 and more fully in FY28, dependent on injectable and Stellon ramp-up.
Two to three new product launches planned annually; a couple of advanced-stage products expected to commercialise in coming quarters.
Injectable facility expected to reach emerging-market sales next year after 12-15 month approval processes.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation: Unit 1 about 80% (analyst later cited 78%); Unit 2 about 25% (analyst later cited 55%); Unit 3 about 55% (includes some KSM manufacturing).
Unit 3 has about 160 acres, with only 20-25% of land used; capacity expansion decision expected at around 80-85% utilisation.
Approximately 1,250 m3 (cited as 1,250-metre cube) fermentation capacity; oncology products run in 5,000-litre fermenters at Unit 1.
Injectable facility: WHO GMP set, validation batches completed, customer audits underway; facility can do close to INR600 crores top line; utilisation about 5%.
Softgel facility added in oral solids; Unit 2 formulation facility at Valthera received NDA Uganda and PPB Kenya inspections; Limbasi facility passed ANVISA inspection.
Possible dedicated fermentation capacity for peptides and veterinary products if growth is needed ahead of the 80-85% threshold.
demand_pricing: Wallet share gains in the quarter were primarily price-driven on existing products, based on economies of scale from fermentation capacity; seeds were sown 8-12 months earlier.
Exports up 46% across Europe, Japan, LatAm and the US; US ANDA approvals received for mycophenolate mofetil and tofacitinib tablets.
Nystatin and fusidic acid (launched FY26, Europe-focused, awaiting CEP) cited as growing products with limited competition.
Management reported no customer concerns on the reported proposed US tariff on generics.
Constant-currency context: USD movement about 10-12% YoY; net impact after input costs about 3-5% flowing to EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How much of growth is normalisation of delayed procurement versus structural gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Some spillover from Q4 FY26 procurement delays contributed; most growth came from new products across all geographies. Similar spillovers are expected in subsequent quarters, though not quantifiable.

qa_highlights.question: Roadmap to INR3,000 crores revenue from existing infrastructure?
qa_highlights.answer: INR600-700 crores from formulations and INR2,200 crores from APIs, expected in about 5-6 years at the current CAGR. Unit 3 has room to expand once utilisation reaches 80-85%.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and CDMO contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 1 about 80%, Unit 3 about 55%, Unit 2 about 25%. CDMO is about 1-2% of revenue, with a target of double digits over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic formulations decline?
qa_highlights.answer: The prior-year quarter included Middle East supplies that did not recur. Ex-Middle East, domestic formulations grew double digits in both divisions.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the wallet share gain attributed to pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing advantage from fermentation scale was passed to customers, and margins were held. Softer factors, such as fermentation partnership, were secondary.

qa_highlights.question: When will the injectable facility reach EBITDA breakeven and emerging-market sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Injectable utilisation is about 5%; breakeven utilisation was not given and will be followed up. Emerging-market sales expected next year after a 12-15 month approval process; contract manufacturing sales expected in 2H FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company reach 40% EBITDA margin by end of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage and renewable energy should drive margins above sales growth. Full 40% depends on injectable and Stellon ramp-up, so it may slip into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How can API revenue reach INR2,200 crores without new capacity, given Unit 1 and Unit 2 utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 3 is the focus for 8-10 pipeline anti-infective and antifungal products. Oncology revenue is high value per litre, so utilisation understates revenue potential. Capacity utilisation for Unit 3 excluding KSMs is slightly above the 20-25% estimate the analyst gave.
